title: The Microscope
description: Nucleus Bot 🤖 powers up the academy's microscopes. Master the tool that reveals the invisible world of cells to earn the first piece of the Cell of Life.

content.value: Cells Are Too Small to See

Most cells are far too small for our eyes to see. To study them, scientists use a MICROSCOPE — an instrument that magnifies (enlarges) tiny objects hundreds or thousands of times so we can examine them.

A microscope uses lenses to bend light and produce a hugely enlarged image of a small object. A thin sample is placed on a glass slide, light shines through it, and the lenses magnify the view. Without it, the whole world of cells would stay hidden.

👁️  eyepiece lens (you look here)
🔎  objective lens (magnifies the sample)
🧪  glass slide with a thin sample
💡  light shines up through the sample

To see cells, the sample must be very THIN so light can pass through it. Scientists often add a drop of a stain (dye) to colour parts of the cell, making them easier to see. A classic school example is peeling the thin skin of an onion to view its neat brick-like cells.
The thinner the sample, the clearer the view — thick samples block the light and look dark. That is why we peel just a single see-through layer, like onion skin.
Key Takeaway: A microscope magnifies tiny objects using lenses and light, letting us see cells. Samples must be thin (and are often stained) so light can pass through and reveal the cells.

quiz.question: A microscope is used to…
options: magnify tiny objects so we can see them
quiz.explain: A microscope magnifies (enlarges) small objects like cells so they can be studied.

quiz.question: Why must a sample be very THIN to view under a microscope?
options: so it fits on the slide
so light can pass through it for a clear image
quiz.explain: Light must pass through the sample; a thin slice gives a clear, bright image.

quiz.question: Scientists often add a stain (dye) to a sample in order to…
options: make parts of the cell easier to see
quiz.explain: Stains colour parts of the cell so they stand out and are easier to observe.
